talks.title: BSidesAugusta 2022 - Keynote: Tim Medin
talks.teaser: Investigates BSidesAugusta 2022 - Keynote: Tim Medin and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
Overview: Tim Medin delivers the BSides Augusta 2022 keynote on credential attacks, sharing decades of penetration testing experience and the enduring importance of credential security.

Key Topics: Kerberos attacks and silver ticket techniques; NSA advisory on Exchange vulnerability exploitation lasting nine months undetected; why credentials lack glamour but remain critical; and Red Siege consulting perspectives.

Technical Details: Medin recounts preparing a Kerberos talk only to have Benjamin Delpy release overlapping silver ticket research the same weekend. He emphasizes that attackers dwelled in Exchange environments for nine months before NSA disclosure in 2020.

Takeaways: Credential attacks remain fundamentally important despite focusing on flashier techniques. Long attacker dwell times on basic vulnerabilities demonstrate persistent defensive failures.

talks.title: Paul Melson - How To Write Good YARA Rules
talks.teaser: Evaluates paul Melson - How To Write Good YARA Rules and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
YARA Foundations

Paul Melson's BSides Augusta workshop teaches writing effective YARA rules—described as a pattern-matching rule engine with human-readable syntax, string and byte patterns, optional file-parser modules, and a Boolean condition block powering flexible logic beyond simple grep.

Rule Structure and Metadata

Every rule declares a name, optional meta fields, a strings section, and conditions tying matches together. Melson stresses metadata—especially author attribution and sample hashes—so future analysts can trace rule provenance and ask informed questions, even though he notes YARA rule release has never paid him directly.

Strings, Modifiers, and Precision

He covers ASCII versus wide (UTF-16) strings, hex byte sequences with wildcards and alternation, and cautions against overly broad conditions that generate noise. Good rules balance specificity with resilience to minor sample variation.

Hands-On Practice

Attendees clone a companion GitHub repository with sample rules and encrypted practice files. Melson promises a live finale where the audience helps author a YARA rule against previously unseen malware, reinforcing iterative, collaborative rule development.

talks.title: Kevin Johnson - hAPI hAPI Joy Joy: Understanding the risks in a world of API integrations
talks.teaser: Reviews kevin Johnson - hAPI hAPI Joy Joy: Understanding the risks in a world of API integrations and evaluates key implications for security practitioners.
talks.summary:
APIs are the future

Kevin Johnson, Secure Ideas founder and OWASP leader, insists APIs are not scary—they are how modern applications integrate. The risk is that teams shipping API-first features rarely understand authorization, exposure, and abuse scenarios they introduce.

Pentesters tell hard truths

Secure Ideas focuses on breaking in, reporting ugly findings, and leaving—no IR or forensics. Johnson uses humor about risk perception (half an Oklahoma BSides audience feared sharks) to argue humans systematically misjudge real versus perceived threats in API design reviews.

Integration sprawl risks

Third-party API keys, overly permissive scopes, and chained integrations create attack paths across services. Johnson urges developers and security teams to threat-model each integration point, assume clients and mobile apps will leak secrets, and validate server-side controls independent of client trust.
